Revenue rises in first quarter

The finance ministry said on Friday that revenue collection rose sharply in the first quarter, driven by higher import duties and stronger corporate tax receipts, while officials cautioned that spending pressures remain.

Economists welcomed the figures but noted that much of the gain came from one-off measures, including a levy on windfall profits at refiners, and warned that growth in the second half could slow as consumer demand softens.

The government has promised to widen the tax net to include wholesale traders and real estate, a reform that previous administrations announced several times without managing to pass through parliament.

Lenders reviewing the country's programme are expected to visit next month, and officials in the capital said they hoped the stronger numbers would help secure the release of the next tranche of financing.

Opposition lawmakers criticised the budget, arguing that indirect taxes fall hardest on low-income households, and called for a debate on spending cuts at the largest state-owned enterprises.
